_note: Toledo v1.1 Lane C, task (1). Question: are the founder's RD1-RD9 identifiers (found, not guessed, in coq/solver-arc/formal/RD.v and its byte-identical public mirror coq/readout_universe/evidence/RD.v -- both header-commented 'Axiom map: RD1 zero, RD2 succ, RD5 induction = Inductive D + elim; RD3 succ<>zero, RD4 succ injective = theorems; RD6,RD7 add ; RD8,RD9 mul = recursive definitions') the SAME OBJECTS as any Genesis root row (E00.1-E00.7 / EQ-001..EQ-008, plus N1-N5 and other named results checked as candidates) under the Toledo equivalence criterion (documented registry/GENESIS_CODE_SCHEME.md / Equivalence Registry design: A = B iff a bijective phi of renaming, fixed positive scale, or fixed constant substitution gives A(x)=B(phi(x)) on the shared domain -- no limits, no approximations)?
method: RD.v (both copies, diffed byte-identical for the shared header+D-construction region) read directly; every genesis_root.json row whose code or alias starts 'E00.' read directly (EQ-001..EQ-008); N1-N5 and the pre-existing GENESIS_CODE_SCHEME.md build note on RD1-RD9 also checked as candidates. No row in genesis_root.json (590 rows) carries a literal 'RD1'..'RD9' code or alias -- confirmed by direct string search, matching the scheme doc's own prior finding.
verdict_key: NOT_SAME_OBJECT = confirmed distinct mathematical object, no phi exists (statements compared directly, quoted both sides); genesis_code is null in every row below because none of the 9 identifiers passed the criterion -- no alias was added anywhere, per the task rule that only confirmed pairs get an alias.

RD1.rd_quote: coq/solver-arc/formal/RD.v (identical in coq/readout_universe/evidence/RD.v), header: "(* ---- RD1, RD2, RD5 ---- *)" then "Inductive D : Type :=\n  | zero : D\n  | succ : D -> D." -- RD1 names the nullary constructor `zero : D` of a from-scratch Peano-style inductive type.
RD1.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-001: name "Primordial difference", statement "\u2203 a,b : a \u2260 b" -- an existence claim about two distinguishable objects, not the introduction of a zero/base term of a number type.
RD1.reasoning: No renaming/scale/constant-substitution bijection carries the term-introduction 'zero : D' onto the existential claim '\u2203 a,b : a\u2260b' -- one is a syntactic constructor of an inductive type, the other is an existence axiom over an unspecified domain of 'distinguishable objects'. Different logical form (term vs. proposition), different arity, different content.

RD2.rd_quote: RD.v: "(* ---- RD1, RD2, RD5 ---- *)" ... "| succ : D -> D." -- RD2 names the unary successor constructor of the same inductive type D.
RD2.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-002: name "Distinguishability needs a distinguisher", statement "\u2203 A : A discriminates E\u2081 \u2260 E\u2082".
RD2.reasoning: RD2 is a type-constructor (a function D -> D at the syntax level, no proposition attached); EQ-002 is an existence claim about a distinguishing agent A. No bijective phi relates a constructor signature to an existential proposition about agents; not the same object under the criterion.

RD3.rd_quote: RD.v: "Theorem RD3_succ_ne_zero : forall x : D, succ x <> zero.\nProof. intros x H. discriminate H. Qed."
RD3.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-003: name "Asymmetry is forced", statement "A\u2192B \u2260 B\u2192A (a directed admissible-transition relation on the retained graph, not material implication)".
RD3.reasoning: RD3 is the Peano successor-not-zero axiom for the constructed type D (a fact about D's two constructors never colliding). EQ-003 asserts that a directed transition relation on a retained graph is asymmetric. Superficially both are '<>'-shaped, but the objects compared (succ x vs. zero; A\u2192B vs. B\u2192A) are not related by any renaming/scale/constant substitution -- one ranges over an inductively built number type, the other over a domain-specific transition relation the source explicitly says is 'not material implication'. Distinct objects.

RD4.rd_quote: RD.v: "Theorem RD4_succ_inj : forall x y : D, succ x = succ y -> x = y.\nProof. intros x y H. congruence. Qed."
RD4.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-004: name "Temporal ordering", statement "t(s) := min #steps(s\u2080 \u2192 s) \u2208 \u2115".
RD4.reasoning: RD4 is successor-injectivity for D. EQ-004 defines a step-count function into the naturals. EQ-004 in fact USES a natural-number codomain (\u2115) rather than stating an axiom equivalent to injectivity of a successor operation; it is a definition of a derived quantity, not a claim about an operator's injectivity. No phi bijection matches the two statements' logical shape (implication over an equality of constructor applications, vs. a definition of a minimum-step function).

RD5.rd_quote: RD.v comment: "RD1, RD2, RD5 ---- Inductive D : Type := | zero : D | succ : D -> D." -- RD5 is the automatically generated structural-induction/elimination principle Coq attaches to this Inductive declaration (D_ind / D_rect), not a separately written theorem in the file.
RD5.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-005: name "Persistence / causal memory", statement "\u03c4_c > 0".
RD5.reasoning: RD5 is a proof-principle (induction) generated by the type declaration; EQ-005 is a strict-positivity claim about a causal-memory time constant \u03c4_c. A proof principle and a numeric-positivity axiom are not comparable under the phi-criterion at all -- different logical categories (a scheme for proofs vs. a ground proposition about a scalar).

RD6.rd_quote: RD.v: "(* ---- RD6, RD7 : addition ---- *)\nFixpoint add (x y : D) : D :=\n  match y with zero => x | succ y' => succ (add x y') end." -- RD6 is the base case `add x zero = x` (see also Lemma add_zero).
RD6.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-006: name "Discrete world before continuum", statement "t = n\u0394\u03b8, n\u2208\u2115, \u0394\u03b8>0 (\u0394\u03b8=0 undefined; continuum is a controlled readout limit)".
RD6.reasoning: RD6 is the recursive-definition base clause for addition on D. EQ-006 states that physical time is an integer multiple of a nonzero discreteness quantum \u0394\u03b8. No renaming/scale/constant substitution turns a definitional equation clause (add x zero = x) into an existential/typing claim about how physical time is built from a quantum step; unrelated content.

RD7.rd_quote: RD.v: same Fixpoint as RD6 -- RD7 is the recursive case `add x (succ y') = succ (add x y')` (see also Lemma add_succ).
RD7.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-007: name "Finite causal propagation speed", statement "v = \u221a(D/\u03c4_c) < \u221e".
RD7.reasoning: RD7 is addition's recursive step on D. EQ-007 bounds a propagation speed computed from a diffusion constant D and \u03c4_c. The two share no common shape (one is a recursive equation defining +1-step addition; the other is a derived-quantity bound with a square root and an explicit finiteness clause) and no phi relates them.

RD8.rd_quote: RD.v: "(* ---- RD8, RD9 : multiplication ---- *)\nFixpoint mul (x y : D) : D :=\n  match y with zero => zero | succ y' => add (mul x y') x end." -- RD8 is the base case `mul x zero = zero` (see also Lemma mul_zero).
RD8.genesis_quote: genesis_root.json EQ-008: name "Retained graph-Laplacian operator L_R", statement "L_R := D_W \u2212 W (D_W = weighted degree matrix, W = retained adjacency; full operator on a multimode retained state, not a scalar)".
RD8.reasoning: RD8 is multiplication's base clause on D (a scalar recursive definition). EQ-008 defines a matrix-valued graph-Laplacian operator L_R on a retained-adjacency graph. A scalar recursive base case and a matrix-operator definition are not the same mathematical object under any renaming/scale/constant-substitution bijection; different types entirely (D -> D vs. an operator on a multimode state space).

RD9.rd_quote: RD.v: same Fixpoint as RD8 -- RD9 is the recursive case `mul x (succ y') = add (mul x y') x` (see also Lemma mul_succ).
RD9.nearest_genesis_candidate: none closer than EQ-008 (no ninth E00.x row exists -- E00.1-E00.7 span EQ-001..EQ-008 only, per genesis_root.json and GENESIS_CODE_SCHEME.md's own note that E00.7 was split into a -speed and -operator pair)
RD9.genesis_quote: n/a -- no distinct ninth root-axiom row exists in genesis_root.json to compare against; the root-axiom stream is exactly E00.1-E00.7 (8 rows, EQ-001..EQ-008 after the E00.7 split), not 9.
RD9.reasoning: RD9 is multiplication's recursive step on D. There is no ninth Genesis root-axiom row at all (the founder's own RD1-RD9 count already does not line up 1:1 with Genesis's 7-tagged/8-row root-axiom stream -- flagged, not resolved, in GENESIS_CODE_SCHEME.md's build notes). Combined with RD1-RD8 all failing the phi-criterion against their nearest candidates, this confirms RD1-RD9 is a wholly separate formal object (a Peano/natural-number construction the corpus calls the 'Retained-Difference object system, machine-checked... Object stratum of "The Roots of Mathematics and Geometry" (Book Zero)', per RD.v's own file banner) and not an alternate naming of the Genesis physical/epistemic root axioms.

summary.closing_note: This resolves the open item flagged in registry/GENESIS_CODE_SCHEME.md ('the founder's shorthand RD1-RD9 for the root axioms does not appear verbatim anywhere in either source file... if RD1-RD9 is a live external naming convention (e.g. from the solver arc, private), reconciling it against E00.1-E00.7 is a follow-up'): RD1-RD9 IS a real, machine-checked, named convention -- found verbatim in coq/solver-arc/formal/RD.v and its byte-identical public mirror coq/readout_universe/evidence/RD.v -- but by direct statement comparison it names a Peano-style natural-number construction (D : Type with zero/succ/add/mul), a different mathematical object from Genesis's E00.1-E00.7 physical/epistemic root axioms. No alias was added to any genesis_root.json row and no coq_map.json code was changed, since zero pairs were confirmed under the phi-criterion. Genesis's own root-axiom identifiers (E00.1-E00.7, i.e. EQ-001..EQ-008 in the Appendix-C stream) remain the sole codes for those axioms, unchanged.
